title: Habré terminado, habría ido: the future and conditional perfect
summary: Habré terminado for done-by-then and guesses, habría ido for what would have been.
focus: The future perfect and the conditional perfect: haber in the future or conditional + participle
content:
## The future perfect: habré terminado

The **futuro perfecto** is the future of **haber** + a participle. It says something will be finished *before* a point in the future: **para el lunes**, **dentro de un mes**, **para entonces**, **cuando llegues**.

| | haber | + participle |
|---|---|---|
| yo | **habré** | terminado |
| tú | **habrás** | comido |
| él / ella / usted | **habrá** | salido |
| nosotros/as | **habremos** | vuelto |
| vosotros/as | **habréis** | hecho |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **habrán** | dicho |

- *Para el lunes habré terminado.* (By Monday I'll have finished.)
- *Cuando llegues, ya habré cenado.* (When you arrive, I'll already have had dinner.)

Irregular participles stay irregular (**hecho, dicho, visto, puesto, vuelto, escrito**), and **no** and pronouns go before haber: *Ya lo habré hecho.*

## Habrá salido: a guess about the recent past

Spanish uses the future to guess: **estará en casa** = he's probably at home. For a guess about something that *has* happened, the future perfect replaces the present perfect:

| sure | a guess |
|---|---|
| **Ha salido.** He has gone out. | **Habrá salido.** He must have gone out. |
| **Se ha dormido.** He has fallen asleep. | **Se habrá dormido.** He must have fallen asleep. |

- *Marcos no contesta. Se habrá quedado sin batería.* (Marcos isn't answering. His battery must have died.)
- *¿Quién habrá llamado tan tarde?* (Who can have called so late?)

English says *must have*, *probably* or *I bet*; Spanish just shifts the tense.

## The conditional perfect: habría ido

| | haber | + participle |
|---|---|---|
| yo | **habría** | ido |
| tú | **habrías** | visto |
| él / ella / usted | **habría** | dicho |
| nosotros/as | **habríamos** | ganado |
| vosotros/as | **habríais** | puesto |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **habrían** | llegado |

The **condicional compuesto** is what *would have* happened but didn't. Often a **pero** gives the reason:

- *Habría ido, pero estaba enfermo.* (I would have gone, but I was ill.)
- *Con un poco más de tiempo, lo habríamos terminado.* (With a bit more time, we'd have finished it.)

For advice about something already done, use **yo que tú** or **yo en tu lugar**: *Yo que tú, lo habría dicho.* (If I were you, I'd have said it.)

## Habría salido ya: a guess about an earlier past

The same shift works one step further back. A guess about what *had* happened, told from the past, swaps the pluperfect for the conditional perfect:

| sure | a guess |
|---|---|
| **Había salido.** He had gone out. | **Habría salido ya.** He must have gone out already. |

- *Cuando llegué, la casa estaba vacía: habrían salido ya.* (When I arrived, the house was empty, so they must have left already.)
- *No vino a la cena. Se le habría olvidado.* (He didn't come to dinner. He must have forgotten.)

Rule of thumb: **ha** becomes **habrá**, and **había** becomes **habría**. The context tells you whether **habría** means *would have* or *must have*.

vocabulary.example: Para el viernes habré leído el libro entero.
vocabulary.example_meaning: By Friday I'll have read the whole book.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Her plane must have landed a while ago.

vocabulary.example_meaning: I don't regret anything, though I'd have done it differently.

vocabulary.example_meaning: If I were you, I'd have asked for a second opinion.

vocabulary.example: Yo en tu lugar no habría vendido el coche.

vocabulary.meaning: thank goodness, it's a good thing that

vocabulary.example: Sin tu mensaje, no me habría enterado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Without your message, I wouldn't have found out.

quiz.prompt: Tranquila: para el lunes (yo) ya ___ el proyecto.
quiz.explanation: Done before a future point (para el lunes) takes the future perfect. Yo takes habré, and haber is always followed by the participle: habré entregado.
hints: Para el lunes looks forward: future, not conditional.

quiz.prompt: Dentro de dos años, mis padres ya ___. (jubilarse, future perfect: 'will have retired')
quiz.explanation: Ellos takes habrán + jubilado, and the reflexive se goes before haber: se habrán jubilado.
hints: The pronoun goes before haber, never between haber and the participle.

quiz.prompt: Ana no contesta al teléfono. ___ el móvil en casa. ('She must have left…')
quiz.explanation: A guess about something that has just happened swaps ha dejado for habrá dejado. Dejará is a plain future (she will leave).
hints: Guessing about the recent past takes the future perfect.

quiz.prompt: A estas alturas, Luis ya ___ a Lisboa. (llegar: 'he'll have arrived by now')
quiz.explanation: A guess about what has probably happened by now: habrá + llegado.

quiz.prompt: Yo ___ a la fiesta, pero tenía fiebre.
quiz.explanation: Something that would have happened but didn't, with pero giving the reason, takes the conditional perfect: habría ido.
hints: Did I go? No, so it is 'would have'.

quiz.prompt: Yo que tú, no ___ ese contrato. (firmar: 'I wouldn't have signed')
quiz.explanation: Advice about something already done: yo que tú + conditional perfect. Yo takes habría firmado.

quiz.prompt: Cuando llegamos a la estación, no había nadie: los demás ya ___. (salir: 'must have left')
quiz.explanation: A guess about an earlier past, told from the past (llegamos, había): the pluperfect habían salido becomes the conditional perfect habrían salido.
hints: The story is in the past, so había becomes habría.

quiz.prompt: Menos mal que me avisaste; de lo contrario, ___ tarde. (llegar, nosotros: 'we would have arrived')
quiz.explanation: What would have happened but didn't: nosotros takes habríamos + llegado. Note the accent on habríamos.
hints: De lo contrario introduces what would have happened.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence says 'By Friday I'll have done it'?
options: Para el viernes lo habré hecho.
Para el viernes habré lo hecho.
Para el viernes lo habré hacido.
quiz.correct_answer: Para el viernes lo habré hecho.
quiz.explanation: The pronoun lo goes before haber, nothing goes between haber and the participle, and hacer has the irregular participle hecho.
hints: Where does lo go in a compound tense?

conversations.title: The Friday deadline
conversations.scenario: Elena and Tomás, two colleagues, are looking for a missing report on a Friday afternoon.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Has visto a Marcos? No está en su mesa.
lines.meaning: Have you seen Marcos? He's not at his desk.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Habrá salido a comer. Siempre se va a las dos.
lines.meaning: He must have gone out for lunch. He always leaves at two.
lines.note: a guess: habrá salido instead of ha salido

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Necesito su informe. ¿Crees que ya lo habrá terminado?
lines.meaning: I need his report. Do you think he'll have finished it yet?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Para el lunes lo habrá terminado, pero hoy lo dudo.
lines.meaning: He'll have finished it by Monday, but today I doubt it.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Qué pena! Yo lo habría hecho en una tarde.
lines.meaning: What a pity! I'd have done it in an afternoon.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ya, pero tú no tenías tres reuniones. Por cierto, ¿por qué no viniste a la de ayer?
lines.meaning: Sure, but you didn't have three meetings. By the way, why didn't you come to yesterday's?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Habría ido, pero mi hijo estaba enfermo. ¿Me perdí algo?
lines.meaning: I would have gone, but my son was ill. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: El jefe cambió los plazos. Yo que tú, ya le habría escrito.
lines.meaning: The boss changed the deadlines. If I were you, I'd have written to him already.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Menos mal que me lo cuentas; de lo contrario, no me habría enterado.
lines.meaning: Thank goodness you're telling me; otherwise I wouldn't have found out.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Escríbele ahora. Para mañana ya habrá decidido todo.
lines.meaning: Write to him now. By tomorrow he'll have decided everything.

listening.text: Ya habrán llegado a casa.
listening.meaning: They'll have got home by now.
listening.note: A guess about the recent past: habrán llegado.

listening.text: Para entonces habré cambiado de trabajo.
listening.meaning: By then I'll have changed jobs.

listening.text: Yo que tú, no habría dicho nada.
listening.meaning: If I were you, I wouldn't have said anything.

listening.text: ¿Dónde está la llave? La habrá cogido tu hermano.
listening.meaning: Where's the key? Your brother must have taken it.
listening.note: New word: la llave = the key.

listening.text: Dentro de veinte años habremos pagado toda la hipoteca.
listening.meaning: In twenty years we'll have paid off the whole mortgage.
listening.note: New word: la hipoteca = the mortgage.

listening.text: Cuando llegué, la cocina estaba limpia: alguien la habría fregado.
listening.meaning: When I arrived, the kitchen was clean: someone must have mopped it.
listening.note: New word: fregar = to mop, to wash up.

listening.text: Habríamos ido a la playa, pero llovió todo el fin de semana.
listening.meaning: We would have gone to the beach, but it rained all weekend.

listening.text: Menos mal que llevabas el mapa; de lo contrario, nos habríamos perdido.
listening.meaning: Good thing you had the map; otherwise we'd have got lost.

guide.tip: Guessing? Step the tense forward. Ha salido becomes habrá salido, and había salido becomes habría salido.

bites.title: Done by then
bites.rule: The future perfect is habré, habrás, habrá… + participle. It is for things finished before a point in the future (para el lunes, dentro de un mes, para entonces).
bites.example: Dentro de un mes habremos vuelto.
bites.example_meaning: In a month we'll have come back.

bites.title: Habrá salido = must have left
bites.rule: Guessing about something that has just happened? Swap the present perfect for the future perfect, so ha salido becomes habrá salido.
bites.example: No abre la puerta: habrá salido.
bites.example_meaning: He's not opening the door: he must have gone out.

bites.title: Would have, but…
bites.rule: The conditional perfect is habría, habrías… + participle. It says what would have happened but didn't. Add pero… for the reason, or yo que tú… for advice.
bites.example: Lo habría comprado, pero era carísimo.
bites.example_meaning: I'd have bought it, but it was really expensive.

bites.title: Habría salido ya = must have left before
bites.rule: Guessing about an earlier past in a story? Swap the pluperfect for the conditional perfect, so había salido becomes habría salido.
bites.example: Cuando llamé, ya se habría acostado.
bites.example_meaning: When I called, she must already have gone to bed.

sorts.title: Habrá or habría?

items.text: done by next Monday
would have gone, but…
must have left just now
if I were you, I'd have said it
will have come back in a year
must have left before I got there yesterday

sorts.why: Habré/habrá looks from now to a future point or guesses about the recent past; habría says what would have been, or guesses further back in a story.

sorts.title: A fact or a guess?

items.text: Ha salido.
Habrá salido.
Había salido.
Habrán cenado ya.
Cuando llamé, ya habrían cenado.
Cuando llegué, se habría ido ya.
Han cenado.

sorts.why: A guess about the recent past turns ha into habrá, and a guess about an earlier past turns había into habría.

spots.sentence: Para el viernes habré terminar el informe.
spots.why: Haber is always followed by the participle, never the infinitive.

spots.sentence: Yo que tú, lo habré dicho antes.
spots.why: Advice about the past (yo que tú) takes the conditional perfect.

spots.sentence: Dentro de un mes habremos volvido de Chile.
spots.why: Volver has an irregular participle: vuelto.

spots.sentence: Ya lo habré hacido para el lunes.
spots.why: Hacer has an irregular participle: hecho.

spots.sentence: Mis padres habríais ido, pero llovía.
spots.why: Mis padres = ellos, so habrían; habríais is vosotros.

builds.text: Para entonces habremos vendido la casa.
builds.meaning: By then we'll have sold the house.

builds.text: Seguro que habrá perdido el autobús.
builds.meaning: He must have missed the bus.

builds.text: Yo en tu lugar no habría aceptado.
builds.meaning: In your place I wouldn't have accepted.

builds.text: Te habrías divertido mucho en la boda.
builds.meaning: You'd have had a great time at the wedding.

realm.content:
## Habré y habría en Eldmark

By dawn your guild **habrá limpiado** the dungeon, finished before a point in the future. The paladin isn't at the inn? **Habrá ido** to Highgate, which is a guess. And the loot you sold too cheaply? **Yo que tú, no lo habría vendido**, which is what would have happened but didn't.

vocabulary.example: Al amanecer, el gremio habrá cruzado el Bosque Umbrío.
vocabulary.example_meaning: By dawn the guild will have crossed the Bosque Umbrío.

vocabulary.example: Para entonces, los enanos habrán forjado tu hacha.
vocabulary.example_meaning: By then the dwarves will have forged your axe.

vocabulary.example: Yo que tú, no habría atacado al minotauro solo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If I were you, I wouldn't have attacked the minotaur alone.

vocabulary.example: Menos mal que trajiste la poción; de lo contrario, habríamos perdido el combate.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Good thing you brought the potion; otherwise we'd have lost the fight.

vocabulary.example: A estas alturas, la maga ya habrá llegado a Frostmarch.
vocabulary.example_meaning: By now the mage will have reached Frostmarch.

vocabulary.example: El gremio habrá elegido ya a su nuevo líder.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The guild must have chosen its new leader by now.

vocabulary.example: Habríamos repartido el botín, pero el orco se lo llevó.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We'd have shared out the loot, but the orc took it.

vocabulary.example: Sin mi montura, habría llegado tarde a la posada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Without my mount, I'd have reached the inn late.

bites.title: Habrá o habría en la misión
bites.rule: A guess about what has just happened: habrá (el cazador habrá vuelto). What would have happened but didn't: habría (habría ganado, pero se rompió mi escudo).
bites.example: Habría ganado el torneo, pero mi montura se cansó.
bites.example_meaning: I'd have won the tournament, but my mount got tired.

listening.text: El enano habrá vuelto a Deepanvil.
listening.meaning: The dwarf must have gone back to Deepanvil.

listening.text: Para entonces, habremos repartido el botín.
listening.meaning: By then we'll have shared out the loot.
listening.note: New word: el botín = the loot.

listening.text: Yo que tú, no habría vendido esa espada.
listening.meaning: If I were you, I wouldn't have sold that sword.
listening.note: New word: la espada = the sword.

listening.text: A estas alturas, el gremio ya habrá cruzado el puente.
listening.meaning: By now the guild will have crossed the bridge.

listening.text: La elfa habría ganado, pero perdió su montura.
listening.meaning: The elf would have won, but she lost her mount.
listening.note: New word: la montura = the mount.

builds.text: El cazador habrá encontrado la mazmorra.
builds.meaning: The hunter must have found the dungeon.

builds.text: Sin tu ayuda, habríamos perdido el botín.
builds.meaning: Without your help, we'd have lost the loot.

spots.sentence: Yo que tú, habré esperado al paladín.
spots.why: Advice about the past takes the conditional perfect.

spots.sentence: Para mañana, la maga habrá aprendo el hechizo.

sorts.title: Habrá or habría in the realm?

items.text: El paladín no está: ___ ido a Highgate.
___ ganado, pero se rompió mi escudo.

sorts.why: Habrá: done by a future point, or a guess about the recent past. Habría: what would have happened but didn't.

quiz.prompt: El paladín no está en la posada. ___ ido a Highgate.
quiz.explanation: A guess about what has just happened (he isn't here now): ha ido becomes habrá ido. Habré is yo.

quiz.prompt: Yo que tú, no ___ el botín tan barato. (vender: 'I wouldn't have sold')
quiz.explanation: Advice about something already done: yo que tú + habría + participle.

conversations.title: The late hunter
conversations.scenario: Maela the mage and Durgo the dwarf wait at the inn for a hunter who is very late.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Durgo, ¿dónde está el cazador? Quedamos a medianoche en la posada.
lines.meaning: Durgo, where's the hunter? We agreed to meet at midnight at the inn.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Habrá encontrado otra mazmorra. Ya sabes cómo es.
lines.meaning: He must have found another dungeon. You know what he's like.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pues yo que tú, no le habría dado el mapa.
lines.meaning: Well, if I were you, I wouldn't have given him the map.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Se lo habría negado, pero me pagó con oro de Deepanvil.
lines.meaning: I'd have refused, but he paid me in Deepanvil gold.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Menos mal; de lo contrario, ya habríamos vendido tu montura.
lines.meaning: Just as well; otherwise we'd have sold your mount by now.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Mira, ahí llega! Se habrá caído en el pantano otra vez.
lines.meaning: Look, here he comes! He must have fallen in the swamp again.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Y para el amanecer se habrá comido todo el pan de la posada.
lines.meaning: And by dawn he'll have eaten all the bread in the inn.

meadowbrook.content:
## Habré y habría en Meadowbrook

By the autumn festival Nora **habrá cosechado** all her pumpkins, finished before a future point. Leo isn't at the river? **Habrá ido** to the tavern, which is a guess. And the strawberries the storm ruined? **Las habría vendido** at Rosa's shop, but it rained, which is what would have happened but didn't.

vocabulary.example: Para el festival, Nora habrá cosechado todas las fresas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: By the festival, Nora will have harvested all the strawberries.

vocabulary.example: Para entonces, las gallinas habrán puesto cien huevos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: By then the hens will have laid a hundred eggs.

vocabulary.example: Dentro de una semana habremos plantado el maíz.
vocabulary.example_meaning: In a week we'll have planted the maize.

vocabulary.example: Yo que tú, habría plantado fresas en primavera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If I were you, I'd have planted strawberries in spring.

vocabulary.example: A estas alturas, Leo ya habrá pescado algo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: By now Leo will have caught something.

vocabulary.example: Menos mal que llovió: de lo contrario, habríamos perdido la cosecha.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Thank goodness it rained: otherwise we'd have lost the harvest.

vocabulary.example: La calabaza de Nora habría ganado el premio, pero se rompió.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora's pumpkin would have won the prize, but it broke.

vocabulary.example: El alcalde habrá visto ya tu huerto nuevo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mayor must have seen your new vegetable patch by now.

bites.title: Habré y habría en la granja
bites.rule: Done by a day on the farm calendar: habré cosechado. A prize you'd have won but didn't: habría ganado, pero…
bites.example: Habría ganado el concurso, pero la vaca se escapó.
bites.example_meaning: I'd have won the contest, but the cow ran off.

listening.text: Leo habrá ido a la taberna.
listening.meaning: Leo must have gone to the tavern.
listening.note: New word: la taberna = the tavern.

listening.text: Para el otoño, habremos cosechado el maíz.
listening.meaning: By autumn we'll have harvested the maize.

listening.text: Rosa habrá cerrado ya la tienda de semillas.
listening.meaning: Rosa must have closed the seed shop by now.

listening.text: Yo que tú, habría plantado más calabazas.
listening.meaning: If I were you, I'd have planted more pumpkins.
listening.note: New word: la calabaza = the pumpkin.

listening.text: Nora habría ido al festival, pero estaba enferma.
listening.meaning: Nora would have gone to the festival, but she was ill.

builds.text: Para el verano habré plantado las fresas.
builds.meaning: By summer I'll have planted the strawberries.

builds.text: Sin lluvia, habríamos perdido la cosecha.
builds.meaning: Without rain, we'd have lost the harvest.

Yo que tú, no habré vendido la vaca.

quiz.prompt: Para el festival de otoño, Nora ya ___ todas las calabazas.

hints: Sure: se ha escapado. A guess?

rustwake.content:
## Habré y habría en el páramo

Before the ash storm the robot gardener **habrá reparado** the antenna, finished before a future point. Leo isn't at the market? **Habrá ido** to the ruined mall, which is a guess. And that Zafiro soda you swapped for ten nuts? **Yo que tú, no la habría cambiado**, which is what would have happened but didn't.

vocabulary.example: Antes de la noche, habremos vuelto a la cúpula.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Before nightfall we'll have gone back to the Dome.

vocabulary.example: Para entonces, el robot jardinero habrá reparado la antena.
vocabulary.example_meaning: By then the robot gardener will have repaired the antenna.

vocabulary.example: Yo que tú, no habría cambiado la gaseosa por diez tuercas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If I were you, I wouldn't have swapped the soda for ten nuts.

vocabulary.example: Menos mal que llevabas agua filtrada: habríamos tenido mucha sed.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Good thing you had filtered water: we'd have been very thirsty.

vocabulary.example: A estas alturas, Leo ya habrá explorado el centro comercial.
vocabulary.example_meaning: By now Leo will have explored the shopping centre.

vocabulary.example: Marta habrá ganado muchas tuercas hoy.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta must have earned a lot of nuts today.

vocabulary.example: Sin el radiorreloj, no me habría enterado de la tormenta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Without the wrist radio, I wouldn't have heard about the storm.

vocabulary.example: La tormenta de ceniza habrá pasado para mañana.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The ash storm will have passed by tomorrow.

bites.title: Habrá y habría en el páramo
bites.rule: Guessing what just happened out there: habrá (Marta habrá cerrado el puesto). What you'd have done but didn't: habría (habría reparado la antena, pero no tenía tuercas).
bites.example: Habría comprado el tónico, pero no tenía tuercas.
bites.example_meaning: I'd have bought the tonic, but I had no nuts.

listening.text: Marta habrá cerrado ya el mercado.
listening.meaning: Marta must have closed the market by now.

listening.text: Para la noche, habremos llegado al taller.
listening.meaning: By nightfall we'll have reached the workshop.

listening.text: El radiorreloj no suena: se habrá roto.
listening.meaning: The wrist radio isn't making a sound: it must have broken.
listening.note: New word: el radiorreloj = the wrist radio.

listening.text: Yo que tú, habría guardado más tuercas.
listening.meaning: If I were you, I'd have kept more nuts.
listening.note: New word: las tuercas = the nuts.

listening.text: Habríamos explorado la gasolinera, pero llegó la tormenta de ceniza.
listening.meaning: We'd have explored the petrol station, but the ash storm came.
listening.note: New word: la tormenta de ceniza = the ash storm.

builds.text: El capataz Ruiz habrá cerrado la cúpula.
builds.meaning: Foreman Ruiz must have closed the Dome.

builds.text: Sin el perro, habríamos perdido las tuercas.
builds.meaning: Without the dog, we'd have lost the nuts.

spots.sentence: Para el viernes habré reparo la antena.
Yo que tú, no habrás bebido ese tónico.
spots.why: Advice about the past: yo que tú + habría + participle.

sorts.title: Habrá or habría in the wasteland?

items.text: Leo no contesta: ___ salido a explorar.
Para la noche, el robot ___ terminado.
___ comprado agua, pero no tenía tuercas.
Yo que tú, no ___ abierto esa puerta.
Antes de la tormenta, ya ___ vuelto a la cúpula.
Sin el radiorreloj, nos ___ perdido.

sorts.why: Habrá: done by a future point, or a guess about the recent past. Habría: what would have happened but didn't.

quiz.prompt: Antes de la tormenta de ceniza, (nosotros) ya ___ a la cúpula.
quiz.explanation: Done before a future point: future perfect. Volver has the irregular participle vuelto.
hints: Antes de la tormenta looks forward.

quiz.prompt: Yo que tú, no ___ la gaseosa Zafiro por diez tuercas. (cambiar: 'I wouldn't have swapped')
quiz.explanation: Advice about something already done: yo que tú + habría + participle.
